recipe: Call `useEffectEvent` only at the top level of your component or inside your own Hooks, never inside loops or conditions.
trigger_condition: You need to create an Effect Event in a React component.
evidence: Call `useEffectEvent` at the top level of your component to create an Effect Event.

recipe: If you need `useEffectEvent` inside a loop or condition, extract a new component and move the Effect Event into it.
trigger_condition: You find yourself wanting to call `useEffectEvent` inside a loop or conditional expression.
evidence: You can't call it inside loops or conditions. If you need that, extract a new component and move the Effect Event into it.

recipe: Only call Effect Event functions from inside Effects or other Effect Events in the same component; do not call them during rendering or pass them to other components or Hooks.
trigger_condition: You are deciding where to invoke an Effect Event function in your component.
evidence: Effect Events can only be called from inside Effects or other Effect Events. Do not call them during rendering or pass them to other components or Hooks.

recipe: Do not use `useEffectEvent` to avoid listing dependencies in your Effect's dependency array; only use it for logic that genuinely should not re-trigger the Effect.
trigger_condition: You are tempted to wrap a value in an Effect Event to keep it out of the dependency array.
evidence: Do not use `useEffectEvent` to avoid specifying dependencies in your Effect's dependency array. This hides bugs and makes your code harder to understand.

recipe: Never include an Effect Event function in a dependency array, since its identity changes on every render and would cause the Effect to re-run unnecessarily.
trigger_condition: You are writing a `useEffect` that calls an Effect Event function.
evidence: Since you can only call them locally and cannot pass them to other components or include them in dependency arrays, a stable identity would serve no purpose, and would actually mask bugs.

recipe: When using `setInterval` or `setTimeout` in an Effect, wrap the callback logic in `useEffectEvent` so it reads the latest render values without restarting the timer on every state change.
trigger_condition: You have a timer in an Effect and need it to read the latest state values without the interval restarting whenever those values change.
evidence: When you use `setInterval` or `setTimeout` in an Effect, you often want to read the latest values from render without restarting the timer whenever those values change.

recipe: When setting up an event listener in an Effect, wrap the listener callback in `useEffectEvent` so it reads the latest render values without the listener being removed and re-added on every state change.
trigger_condition: You need an event listener in an Effect that depends on state values you do not want to cause the listener to be re-registered.
evidence: When you set up an event listener in an Effect, you often need to read the latest values from render in the callback. Without `useEffectEvent`, you would need to include the values in your dependencies, causing the listener to be removed and re-added on every change.

recipe: Wrap callbacks in useEffectEvent within custom hooks to prevent Effects from re-running when a new callback is passed in on every render.
trigger_condition: You are building a custom hook that sets up an Effect (such as an interval or subscription) and accepts a callback parameter that may change identity each render.
evidence: You can use `useEffectEvent` inside your own custom Hooks. This lets you create reusable Hooks that encapsulate Effects while keeping some values non-reactive:

recipe: If you need to run logic during render, don't wrap it in useEffectEvent. Call the logic directly or move it into an Effect.
trigger_condition: You are getting the error "A function wrapped in useEffectEvent can't be called during rendering".
evidence: If you need to run logic during render, don't wrap it in `useEffectEvent`. Call the logic directly or move it into an Effect.

recipe: Remove Effect Events from dependency arrays of useEffect to avoid the Effect re-running on every render.
trigger_condition: You are getting a lint error "Functions returned from useEffectEvent must not be included in the dependency array".
evidence: Effect Events are designed to be called from Effects without being listed as dependencies. The linter enforces this because the function identity is [intentionally not stable](#why-are-effect-events-not-stable). Including it would cause your Effect to re-run on every render.

recipe: If you need a callback for event handlers or to pass to children, use a regular function or useCallback instead of useEffectEvent.
trigger_condition: You are getting a lint error "... is a function created with useEffectEvent, and can only be called from Effects".
evidence: If you need a callback for event handlers or to pass to children, use a regular function or `useCallback` instead.
